content.title: About
content.content: Pfeffernusse are traditional German ginger spice cookies, small round biscuits glazed with sugar. They have a slightly crunchy edge and a soft, aromatic interior, flavored with ginger, cinnamon, clove and sometimes a hint of pepper.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Pfeffernusse are traditionally baked in the weeks leading up to Christmas and often given as holiday gifts.
The name comes from the German words “Pfeffer” (pepper) and “Nusse” (nut), although the recipe usually contains no nuts.
The recipe dates back to the 16th‑17th centuries, when spices were a luxury item.
Original versions use ground ginger, cinnamon, clove, cardamom and occasionally ground black pepper.
In some regions the cookies are finished with a thin sugar glaze and sometimes sprinkled with chopped nuts.

items.title: Rich in spices
items.content: Ginger and cinnamon have antioxidant and anti‑inflammatory properties that can support immune health.

items.title: Source of minerals
items.content: The spice blend provides small amounts of iron, magnesium and manganese.

items.title: Moderate sugar content
items.content: Small servings deliver quick energy without excessive sugar overload.

items.title: Spice allergy
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to ginger, cinnamon or clove.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: People with diabetes should monitor portion size due to the added sugar.

items.title: High calorie density
items.content: Because of butter and sugar, the cookies are calorie‑dense; moderation is recommended.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Pfeffernusse can be enjoyed as a snack, served with tea or coffee, used as decorative toppings for cakes and cupcakes, or crumbled into ice cream.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. For longer shelf life keep them in the refrigerator to preserve their crisp texture and spice aroma.
